newsitem.title: UK: WS Atkins up on Hong Kong contract award.
newsitem.headline: WS Atkins up on Hong Kong contract award.

text.p: Shares in engineering consultancy WS Atkins Plc rose on Monday after the company said its Hong Kong unit won a consultancy contract on a HK$75 billion project to build a railway linking south China and Hong Kong.
The stock, which floated on the London Stock Exchange in July, was up 15p at 322-1/2 by 1305 GMT in thin trade of just 63,453 shares, after earlier touching a record 325p.
In a statement, Atkins chief executive Michael Jeffries said the contract was a "major breakthrough in our efforts to develop and expand our business in the Asia Pacific region."
He said Atkins' work would include the geological site investigation of three sections of the route, three major urban stations along with land reclamation and the relocation of ferry piers.
The railway, which will serve mixed heavy freight, inter-city passenger and local commuter requirements, will link the southern peninsula of China at Kowloon with the Hong Kong border.
